record.context_brief: Associativity of the asymptotic Hecke algebra
record.original_question: Assume the boundedness statement in problem (b): there is an integer N >= 0 such that v^{-N} h_{x,y,z} is in Z[v^{-1}] for all x, y, z in W, where the Kazhdan-Lusztig basis elements satisfy c_x c_y = sum_{z in W} h_{x,y,z} c_z. For each z in W, let a(z) be the unique integer such that every h_{x,y,z} lies in v^{a(z)} Z[v^{-1}] and for some x, y the coefficient h_{x,y,z} does not lie in v^{a(z)-1} Z[v^{-1}]. Then define integers gamma_{x,y,z^{-1}} by h_{x,y,z} = gamma_{x,y,z^{-1}} v^{a(z)} mod v^{a(z)-1} Z[v^{-1}], let J be the free abelian group with basis {t_w ; w in W}, and define multiplication by t_x t_y = sum_{z in W} gamma_{x,y,z^{-1}} t_z. Does this multiplication always define an associative ring structure on J, even when J has no unit in general?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let (W, S) be a Coxeter system, and let H be the associated Iwahori–Hecke algebra over Z[v, v^{-1}], with standard basis {T_w : w ∈ W} satisfying the usual quadratic and braid relations. Let {c_w : w ∈ W} denote the Kazhdan–Lusztig basis of H, and define structure constants h_{x,y,z} ∈ Z[v, v^{-1}] by

    c_x c_y = ∑_{z ∈ W} h_{x,y,z} c_z,    for all x, y ∈ W.

Assume the following boundedness hypothesis:

(B) There exists an integer N ≥ 0 such that v^{-N} h_{x,y,z} ∈ Z[v^{-1}] for all x, y, z ∈ W.

Under hypothesis (B), for each z ∈ W there is a unique integer a(z) ≥ 0 such that

    h_{x,y,z} ∈ v^{a(z)} Z[v^{-1}]   for all x, y ∈ W,

and h_{x,y,z} ∉ v^{a(z)-1} Z[v^{-1}] for some x, y ∈ W. For x, y, z ∈ W, define integers γ_{x,y,z^{-1}} ∈ Z by the congruence

    h_{x,y,z} ≡ γ_{x,y,z^{-1}} · v^{a(z)}   (mod v^{a(z)-1} Z[v^{-1}]).

Let J be the free abelian group with basis {t_w : w ∈ W}, and define a Z-bilinear product on J by

    t_x · t_y = ∑_{z ∈ W} γ_{x,y,z^{-1}} t_z,    for all x, y ∈ W.

Prove that this product is associative, so that J becomes an associative ring (not necessarily having a multiplicative unit).

status_evidence.title: Remarks on the asymptotic Hecke algebra
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses Lusztig's construction of the asymptotic Hecke algebra J under boundedness assumptions and conjectures P1–P15.
status_evidence.claim: The associativity of J as a consequence of boundedness is part of Lusztig's framework of conjectures P1–P15, which remain conjectural for general Coxeter groups.

status_evidence.title: Three pictures of Lusztig's asymptotic Hecke algebra (Dawydiak thesis)
status_evidence.snippet: Reviews the construction of J and notes that Lusztig's conjectures P1–P15, including those needed for associativity, are known for finite and affine Weyl groups but open in general.
status_evidence.claim: Associativity of J is known in finite and affine Weyl group cases but open in general for Coxeter groups.

artifact.status_search_result: Lusztig's construction of the asymptotic ring J and the question of its associativity given the boundedness conjecture (B) is part of the conjectural framework P1–P15. Associativity has been established for finite Coxeter groups and for affine Weyl groups (with equal parameters), but for general Coxeter groups the statement remains open. No source found showing a proof in full generality.
